plugins.name: conversational-context-transfer
plugins.description: Guides structured conversational extraction to build rich, Claude-optimized context documents about people, projects, or domains

plugins.name: structured-conversation-output-style
plugins.description: Output style for dialogue-driven work: context transfer, design discussions, brainstorming. Conversational thinking partner with file-as-working-memory discipline.

plugins.name: logseq-interface
plugins.description: Agentic Logseq graph access via the logseq CLI — defers to the CLI's self-documentation and adds environment defaults plus graph semantics the CLI does not explain.

plugins.name: design-doc-evals
plugins.description: Authors the Testing & Evaluation section of a software design document — derives the checkable assertions from your Vision, Goal State, Guiding Principles, and Technical Spec, then surfaces the judgment calls (thresholds, acceptance bars) as questions rather than confabulating them.

plugins.name: design-patterns
plugins.description: Design patterns for authoring Claude Code skills — currently: constructing tacit-knowledge skills that load a source text verbatim as framing context rather than distilling it into procedures.

plugins.name: tacit-frames
plugins.description: Tacit-knowledge skills — each loads one source text verbatim as ambient framing context rather than distilling it into procedures. Currently: Anthropic's "Demystifying evals for AI agents".

plugins.name: eval-harness
plugins.description: Evaluate a system by having a real, controlled Claude instance operate it — a reference scenario runtime for the Claude Agent SDK (multi-turn sessions, deterministic gates, sandboxing, transcript and cost capture), plus the SDK's undocumented behavioral facts, each version-stamped and shipped with an executable check rather than asserted from memory.

plugins.name: ask-matt
plugins.description: Ask which skill or flow fits your situation. A router over the skills in this repo.

plugins.name: claude-handoff
plugins.description: Hand the current conversation off to a fresh background agent that picks up the work immediately.

plugins.name: code-review
plugins.description: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes: Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".

plugins.name: codebase-design
plugins.description: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.

plugins.name: diagnosing-bugs
plugins.description: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.

plugins.name: domain-modeling
plugins.description: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or editing a CONTEXT.md, or recording or editing an ADR.

plugins.name: git-guardrails-claude-code
plugins.description: Set up Claude Code hooks to block dangerous git commands (push, reset --hard, clean, branch -D, etc.) before they execute. Use when user wants to prevent destructive git operations, add git safety hooks, or block git push/reset in Claude Code.

plugins.name: grill-me
plugins.description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design.

plugins.name: grill-with-docs
plugins.description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design, which also creates docs (ADR's and glossary) as we go.

plugins.name: grilling
plugins.description: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.

plugins.name: handoff
plugins.description: Compact the current conversation into a handoff document for another agent to pick up.

plugins.name: implement
plugins.description: Implement a piece of work based on a spec or set of tickets.

plugins.name: implement-spec
plugins.description: Implement a specification in code.

plugins.name: improve-codebase-architecture
plugins.description: Scan a codebase for deepening opportunities, present them as a visual HTML report, then grill through whichever one you pick.

plugins.name: loop-me
plugins.description: Grill me about specs for the workflows I want to build, within this workspace.

plugins.name: migrate-to-shoehorn
plugins.description: Migrate test files from `as` type assertions to @total-typescript/shoehorn. Use when user mentions shoehorn, wants to replace `as` in tests, or needs partial test data.

plugins.name: prototype
plugins.description: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.

plugins.name: research
plugins.description: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.

plugins.name: resolving-merge-conflicts
plugins.description: Use when you need to resolve an in-progress git merge/rebase conflict.

plugins.name: retro
plugins.description: Conduct a retrospective on a coding session.

plugins.name: scaffold-exercises
plugins.description: Create exercise directory structures with sections, problems, solutions, and explainers that pass linting. Use when user wants to scaffold exercises, create exercise stubs, or set up a new course section.

plugins.name: setup-matt-pocock-skills
plugins.description: Configure this repo for the engineering skills: set up its issue tracker, triage label vocabulary, and domain doc layout. Run once before first use of the other engineering skills.

plugins.name: setup-pre-commit
plugins.description: Set up Husky pre-commit hooks with lint-staged (Prettier), type checking, and tests in the current repo. Use when user wants to add pre-commit hooks, set up Husky, configure lint-staged, or add commit-time formatting/typechecking/testing.

plugins.name: setup-ts-deep-modules
plugins.description: Wire dependency-cruiser into a TypeScript repo so each package is a deep module, with implementation hidden in subfolders and reachable only through its entry-point files. User-invoked.

plugins.name: tdd
plugins.description: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.

plugins.name: teach
plugins.description: Teach the user a new skill or concept, within this workspace.

plugins.name: to-questionnaire
plugins.description: Turn a decision you can't fully answer into a questionnaire for someone else to fill in.

plugins.name: to-spec
plugins.description: Turn the current conversation into a spec and publish it to the project issue tracker: no interview, just synthesis of what you've already discussed.

plugins.name: to-tickets
plugins.description: Break a plan, spec, or the current conversation into a set of tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its blocking edges, published to the configured tracker (edges as text in one file per ticket locally, or native blocking links on a real tracker).

plugins.name: triage
plugins.description: Move issues and external PRs through a state machine of triage roles, categorise, verify, grill if needed, and write agent-ready briefs.

plugins.name: wait-what
plugins.description: Stop. That last message did not land: re-pitch it.

plugins.name: wayfinder
plugins.description: Plan a huge chunk of work (more than one agent session can hold) as a shared map of decision tickets on your issue tracker, and resolve them one at a time until the way to the destination is clear.

plugins.name: wizard
plugins.description: Generate an interactive bash wizard that walks a human through steps only they can perform. Use when provisioning infrastructure, setting up credentials or CI secrets, walking an unfamiliar third-party dashboard, or running a one-off migration or cutover. Don't invoke this for steps the agent can perform itself.

plugins.name: writing-beats
plugins.description: Writing, exploit; assemble raw material into a journey of beats, grounding each term before a beat leans on it.

plugins.name: writing-for-agents
plugins.description: Writing documents for agents. Use when creating or editing skills, or modifying AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.

plugins.name: writing-fragments
plugins.description: Writing, explore: mine raw fragments, no structure yet.

plugins.name: writing-shape
plugins.description: Writing, exploit: shape raw material into an article, paragraph by paragraph.
